assessment: The incumbent supports telephone and in-person booking, staffed key collection, and substantial recurring access: eleven groups obtained weekly bookings. Its strongest plausible account is that familiar human coordination serves most groups while preserving predictable reservations. It has not demonstrated the target: three conflicts occurred and administration averaged 127.5 minutes weekly; total needs and acceptable windows are unknown. A concrete limit on interpreting 68% reservation as spare usable capacity is the only acoustic piano: seven bookings required it, while other equipment needs were blank. Concentrated evening requests further limit substitutability. Late starts or absences do not establish that bookings could safely be reassigned.

openings.claim: Does unreserved capacity actually match unmet rehearsal needs once acceptable windows, duration, and equipment are recorded?
openings.delta: Distinguish allocation mismatch from scarcity of a particular room or time; aggregate utilization cannot make that distinction.
openings.prediction: An allocation mismatch would leave feasible assignments for previously unsuccessful groups; constrained scarcity would leave requests unmatched even after voluntary changes to inherited slots.
openings.probe: Use the short contact conversations to record complete weekly needs, acceptable windows, equipment, and the outstanding needs of groups rehearsing elsewhere. Attempt a paper allocation within existing hours and equipment, protecting both performances and every requested weekly 60-minute entitlement. Count matched stated needs without treating outside rehearsals or shortened sessions as substitutes without agreement.
assumptions: Contacts can describe group needs accurately.
Allocation is initially a feasibility exercise; any changes require confirmed agreement.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: one authoritative desk calendar, booking identifiers, and recorded confirmation of every change would reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.delta: Replace independently actionable copies with one commitment record; retain the online calendar as a dated informational copy.
openings.prediction: Calendar disagreements should cease causing conflicts; if duplicate arrivals persist despite matching confirmed identifiers, misunderstanding or another access process needs investigation. Administration may increase.
openings.probe: For two weeks, require volunteer and desk changes to reach the authoritative paper record before telephone or in-person confirmation; read back room, date, time, and identifier. Log conflicts, amendment effort, and whether participants relied on stale information. Continue only if the procedure supports the administration target.
assumptions: Existing telephone coordination can synchronize volunteer and desk without additional staffing.
Participants can retain a verbal or paper confirmation without an account.
